title: JSX
summary: JSX is a syntax extension that lets you write HTML-like markup inside JavaScript. It is compiled to React.createElement() calls under the hood. JSX expressions must return a single root element — use a fragment (<>...</>) when you need to return siblings without adding a wrapper div. JavaScript expressions go inside curly braces {}. JSX attributes use camelCase (className, onClick, htmlFor) instead of HTML attributes.
keyPoints: JSX compiles to React.createElement() calls — it is not HTML
Every JSX expression must have exactly one root element or use a fragment <>...</>
Embed JavaScript expressions inside curly braces: {variable}, {fn()}, {a + b}
HTML attributes use camelCase: className instead of class, htmlFor instead of for, onClick instead of onclick
Self-closing tags must have a slash: , ,
Comments in JSX: {/* this is a comment */}
JSX prevents injection attacks — values are escaped before rendering

exercises.prompt: Which of these is valid JSX?
exercises.explanation: JSX uses className instead of class. The closing tag must match exactly. While <DIV> would technically work in JSX (it compiles), React treats uppercase tags as components, not HTML elements.

exercises.prompt: How do you embed a JavaScript variable in JSX?
exercises.explanation: Single curly braces {} are used to embed JavaScript expressions in JSX. Double braces {{}} are used for inline style objects, not variable interpolation.

The elements are automatically wrapped in a div
exercises.answer: A syntax error — JSX must have one root element
exercises.explanation: JSX requires a single root element. Wrap siblings in a <div> or use a fragment <>...</> to avoid adding extra DOM nodes.

exercises.prompt: Which correctly returns siblings without adding a wrapper element to the DOM?
exercises.explanation: Fragments (<>...</>) group elements without adding an extra DOM node. A div wrapper works but adds unnecessary markup. Arrays work technically but require keys and are not idiomatic.

exercises.prompt: Which is the correct way to write a comment inside JSX?
exercises.explanation: JSX comments must be wrapped in curly braces as JavaScript expressions: {/* comment */}. HTML comments and bare JS comments are not valid inside JSX markup.

exercises.prompt:
What does JSX compile to under the hood?

<button className="btn">Click</button>
exercises.explanation: JSX is syntactic sugar for React.createElement(type, props, ...children). The compiler transforms JSX into these function calls before the browser runs the code.

exercises.prompt: Fix this JSX so it renders a label with the text 'Email' pointing to an input with id 'email':
exercises.explanation: In JSX, the 'for' attribute is written as 'htmlFor' (since for is a reserved word in JavaScript), and void elements like <input> must be self-closing with />.
